Ahri.watch: If Ahri E Charm hits, you may take the full follow-up damage, so move behind minions. Ahri Q Orb of Deception can also hit on its return, so keep moving out of its return path even after dodging the first pass.
Ahri.build: Early, buy Null-Magic Mantle to survive and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Most of Ahri's damage is magic, so build magic resistance first, but resistance cannot reduce the true damage from the return of Ahri Q Orb of Deception. If healing from Ahri P Essence Theft keeps offsetting the damage over time from Anivia R Glacial Storm, reduce her healing with Morellonomicon.
Ahri.fight: Do not spend Anivia Q Flash Frost carelessly on poke. Use it to trade after dodging Ahri E Charm. When Ahri R Spirit Rush is down, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize and look for a chance to land Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Ahri.combo: For a basic trade, cast Anivia Q Flash Frost, reactivate it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite. While Ahri R Spirit Rush is down, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, then follow with Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not use an unempowered Anivia E Frostbite.
Ahri.escape: If Ahri E Charm is also down, use Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize from among the minions to limit Ahri's escape routes.
Ahri.phase: Late game, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Ahri.teamfight: Stay well behind your frontline and place Anivia R Glacial Storm at the fight location early so it grows to full size. Dodge Ahri E Charm while using Anivia W Crystallize to separate enemy reinforcements, then hit enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. In narrow passages, use the wall to divide the terrain without blocking allies who are moving in.

Akali.watch: Prioritize dodging the first shuriken from Akali E Shuriken Flip. If it marks you, the second dash will follow Anivia as she retreats, so stay alert for an engage with Akali R Perfect Execution even after dodging the shuriken. You can throw Anivia Q Flash Frost during the brief moment Akali is revealed as she enters Akali W Twilight Shroud.
Akali.build: Early, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Akali's main damage is magic and Anivia has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Also get enough health to withstand the second hit of Akali R Perfect Execution.
Akali.fight: Save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop Akali's engage or for a clear chance to land it. If only one of Akali W Twilight Shroud, Akali E Shuriken Flip, or Akali R Perfect Execution is down, watch for her remaining mobility, and look especially for an opening before Akali R Perfect Execution comes back up. Use Anivia E Frostbite after chilling her with Anivia Q Flash Frost to deal empowered damage.
Akali.laning: Focus on dodging the first shuriken from Akali E Shuriken Flip. If you have pushed the wave, save Anivia W Crystallize for your escape.
Akali.combo: The basic trade is Anivia Q Flash Frost → reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost for an early detonation → Anivia E Frostbite. If you can block Akali's escape, place Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite.
Akali.escape: Before Akali R Perfect Execution comes back up is Anivia's chance to engage. If only Akali W Twilight Shroud or Akali E Shuriken Flip is down, account for her remaining mobility. As you engage, block her escape with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize.
Akali.phase: Anivia gains strength in mid game as her mana problems ease. Late game, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Akali.teamfight: Stay well behind your frontline and place Anivia R Glacial Storm at the fight location early so it grows to full size. When Akali engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate enemy reinforcements, then attack enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. Look for fights in narrow passages, but place the wall so it does not block allies who are moving in.

Akshan.watch: Akshan Q Avengerang gains range when it hits minions, so do not stand behind the wave and dodge both its outward and return paths. Akshan E Heroic Swing uses walls to engage, so keep your distance near walls. Right after he uses it, block his escape with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize. If you are low on health and the targeting indicator for Akshan R Comeuppance appears, move behind terrain.
Akshan.build: Akshan's main damage is physical and Anivia has low armor, so build armor first. Early, survive with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots.
Akshan.fight: Early, keep your distance and farm CS instead of looking for a kill. Right after you make Akshan use Akshan E Heroic Swing is your chance to close the gap: block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and land Anivia Q Flash Frost. Continue the trade with Anivia E Frostbite only if Q hits.
Akshan.laning: Do not keep standing behind the wave, where Akshan Q Avengerang can gain range by hitting minions. If you have pushed the wave, save Anivia W Crystallize for an engage with Akshan E Heroic Swing.
Akshan.combo: When Akshan E Heroic Swing is down, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize, reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Q misses, do not force an E without the chill. If you can place Anivia R Glacial Storm before the fight, wait until it reaches full size before following with Q and E.
Akshan.escape: Engage right after Akshan E Heroic Swing is used. Stun him with Anivia Q Flash Frost and block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize to give him less room to get out.
Akshan.phase: Anivia gains strength from mid game as her mana problems ease. Late game, control terrain with her wall and storm.
Akshan.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm at the fight location early and let it grow. If Akshan engages with Akshan E Heroic Swing, use Anivia W Crystallize to cut off enemy reinforcements, then hit enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. If you have a Scoundrel mark, avoid facing Akshan alone and fight outside his finishing range.

Annie.watch: When white light swirls around Annie, Annie P Pyromania's stun is ready. Stay outside her ability range. In teamfights, Annie R Summon: Tibbers can land with the stun, so do not group tightly with allies when Annie is out of sight or her stun is ready. After Tibbers is summoned, do not stay there even if you kill Annie.
Annie.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Annie deals mostly magic damage, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Annie.fight: After Annie P Pyromania's stun is spent, keep your distance and start trades with Anivia Q Flash Frost. Follow with Anivia E Frostbite only if Q hits and chills her. If Annie steps forward, use Anivia W Crystallize to block her retreat and set up Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Annie.laning: When Annie P Pyromania's stun is ready, stay outside its range. Save Anivia Q Flash Frost for stopping ganks or a guaranteed hit rather than poke. Even after learning Anivia R Glacial Storm, push the wave only for a purpose, such as roaming or gaining vision, and turn it off immediately afterward.
Annie.combo: For a basic trade, hit Annie with Anivia Q Flash Frost, recast it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If you can cut off her escape, block it with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, then follow with Anivia E Frostbite. Save Anivia E Frostbite if Anivia Q Flash Frost misses.
Annie.escape: Move in to pressure Annie just after she spends Annie P Pyromania's stun. Annie has no mobility ability, so use that opening to block her retreat with Anivia W Crystallize and line up Anivia Q Flash Frost. Annie E Molten Shield grants movement speed, so account for her direction of travel when placing the wall.
Annie.phase: In the late game, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm while staying alert for Annie's stun engage.
Annie.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. If Annie is out of sight or Annie P Pyromania's stun is ready, do not group tightly with allies. Decide in advance who will respond when Annie steps forward to engage with Annie R Summon: Tibbers. Once she engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate the follow-up, then hit enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

Aurora.watch: If Aurora Q Twofold Hex hits you, move off the line between you and Aurora to reduce the return damage. The return damage increases as your health falls, so do not try to hold out while cursed. Decide whether to retreat or fight inside the area before Aurora R Between Worlds appears.
Aurora.build: Aurora deals mainly magic damage, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance. Early on, survive with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. If healing from Aurora P Spirit Abjuration keeps offsetting the damage over time from Anivia R Glacial Storm, consider Morellonomicon.
Aurora.fight: When Aurora uses Aurora W Across the Veil, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where she might arrive while waiting for her stealth to end. If Aurora uses her mobility to engage and has fewer ways out, block her retreat with Anivia W Crystallize and hit her with Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Aurora.laning: If you push the lane, keep Anivia W Crystallize available to block the route behind you when you retreat.
Aurora.combo: For a basic trade, hit Aurora with Anivia Q Flash Frost, recast it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If you can block her retreat with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not force Anivia E Frostbite.
Aurora.escape: Do not engage just because Aurora W Across the Veil is down. Look for a chance to catch Aurora with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize if she has used her mobility to engage and has not reset its cooldown through a takedown, especially before Aurora R Between Worlds is available again.
Aurora.phase: In the late game, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Aurora.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it reach full size. When Aurora engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate the follow-up, then hit the target left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. Aurora can leap again after a takedown, so do not leave low-health allies behind when retreating.

AurelionSol.watch: Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light deals damage based on maximum health and builds Stardust if it hits you for long enough. Stand behind minions and move out of its line of fire quickly. When low on health, beware the execute from Aurelion Sol E Singularity. In the late game, spread out so multiple allies are not hit by Aurelion Sol R Falling Star / The Skies Descend.
AurelionSol.build: Early on, survive with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Aurelion Sol's main damage is magic, so prioritize magic resistance on Anivia. Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light deals damage based on maximum health, so be wary of building only a large amount of health.
AurelionSol.fight: Keep your distance and avoid Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light. Counterattack just after he uses Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight. Block his retreat with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not force an unempowered Anivia E Frostbite.
AurelionSol.laning: Avoid Aurelion Sol Q Breath of Light from behind minions. Save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop engages or for clear fight opportunities rather than poke. If you push the lane, keep Anivia W Crystallize available to protect your escape route.
AurelionSol.combo: When Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is down, block his retreat with Anivia W Crystallize, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall to stun him, then use Anivia E Frostbite. Anivia Q Flash Frost must chill him for Anivia E Frostbite to deal double damage. If you have placed Anivia R Glacial Storm early and let it reach full size, you can also use its chill to empower Anivia E Frostbite.
AurelionSol.escape: Just after you force Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is your chance to close the gap. Catch him with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia Q Flash Frost. If you enter Aurelion Sol E Singularity, move out immediately instead of continuing the fight.
AurelionSol.phase: Keep last-hitting and use openings when Aurelion Sol W Astral Flight is down to limit his growth. Anivia becomes stronger in the mid game as her mana issues ease, but Aurelion Sol P Cosmic Creator stacks permanently, making him harder to catch with the same fight opportunities in the late game.
AurelionSol.teamfight: From behind her frontline, Anivia places Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and lets it grow. When Aurelion Sol engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate the follow-up, then hit the opponent left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. In the late game, keep space between you and your allies so you are not hit together by Aurelion Sol R Falling Star / The Skies Descend.

Azir.watch: Do not stand for long in line with soldiers placed by Azir W Arise!; move to the side. Azir Q Conquering Sands slows, so check the soldiers' positions immediately after he moves them. If Azir R Emperor's Divide hits your team in a narrow passage, it can push back those engaging and block those following.
Azir.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Azir's magic damage. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Against Azir, build magic resistance over armor.
Azir.fight: If Azir's soldiers are stationary and he has used Azir Q Conquering Sands, move around the soldiers for a short trade. Hit him with Anivia Q Flash Frost to chill him, then use Anivia E Frostbite. Save E if Q misses. A long fight exposes you to repeated soldier damage, so deal damage quickly when you catch Azir.
Azir.laning: Do not waste Anivia Q Flash Frost on poke. Save it to stop Azir's engage or a jungler's intervention.
Azir.combo: Place Anivia W Crystallize along Azir's retreat path, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. In teamfights, place Anivia R Glacial Storm first and let it reach full size before following with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. If the full-size storm chills Azir, Anivia E Frostbite is empowered even without Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Azir.escape: Just after you force Azir E Shifting Sands is your chance to close the gap. Block his retreat with Anivia W Crystallize and catch him with Anivia Q Flash Frost. If Azir places a soldier beyond the wall, he can use E toward it to escape, so check his escape direction first.
Azir.phase: Anivia becomes stronger in the mid game as her mana issues ease. In the late game, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm. Azir also grows stronger as the game goes on, so catch him briefly and finish him in fights.
Azir.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. Do not enter a narrow passage as a group, or Azir R Emperor's Divide may push multiple allies back together. When the enemy engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate the follow-up, then hit enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

Corki.watch: Corki R Missile Barrage also damages targets around the first target hit, so move out of range instead of hiding behind minions. Reposition to avoid taking consecutive missiles, especially the third. Corki E Gatling Gun reduces your armor and magic resistance when it hits, so move to the side instead of holding your ground in front of him.
Corki.build: Early on, sustain through lane with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Build armor first against Corki's main damage, but prioritize moving out of the position in front of him where Corki E Gatling Gun can reach you. Resistances cannot reduce the true damage from Corki P Hextech Munitions.
Corki.fight: Do not force a close fight while Corki W Valkyrie is available. Right after Corki uses Corki W Valkyrie, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and fight after landing Anivia Q Flash Frost. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite.
Corki.laning: Save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop ganks and capitalize after Corki W Valkyrie is down. Once you learn Anivia R Glacial Storm, push the wave when you intend to roam or establish vision, then turn it off immediately.
Corki.combo: When Corki W Valkyrie is down, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. In teamfights, place Anivia R Glacial Storm first and let it grow to full size before following with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.
Corki.escape: Right after Corki uses Corki W Valkyrie is your chance to close the gap or catch him out. Use Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize to restrict his movement then.
Corki.phase: Late game, use Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm to control the terrain so Corki cannot fire missiles from a safe position.
Corki.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm early where the fight will happen and let it grow. When the enemy engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate their follow-up, then hit the enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. Fight in narrow passages, but place the wall so it does not block allies who are engaging.

Ekko.build: Ekko's damage is mostly magic, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Buy Null-Magic Mantle early and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Ekko.fight: For a basic trade, land Anivia Q Flash Frost to chill Ekko, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save mana and do not use Anivia E Frostbite. Right after Ekko closes in with Ekko E Phase Dive, respond with the stun from Anivia Q Flash Frost or with Anivia W Crystallize.
Ekko.laning: Save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop engages with Ekko E Phase Dive and ganks instead of using it to poke. Even after learning Anivia R Glacial Storm, push the wave only for a purpose such as roaming or securing vision, then turn it off immediately.
Ekko.combo: Block Ekko's escape with Anivia W Crystallize, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. While Ekko is stunned by Anivia Q Flash Frost, place Anivia R Glacial Storm to keep dealing damage. If you placed Anivia R Glacial Storm first, wait for it to reach full size before using Anivia E Frostbite on the chilled Ekko.
Ekko.escape: After avoiding the stun from Ekko W Parallel Convergence and once Ekko E Phase Dive is down, you have a chance to catch him with Anivia Q Flash Frost. If Ekko R Chronobreak is down too, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and engage. If you can see an afterimage behind Ekko, Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, so do not overcommit to chasing him even when health is low.
Ekko.phase: Late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm instead of chasing Ekko.
Ekko.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm early where the fight will happen and let it reach full size. If Ekko engages with Ekko E Phase Dive, stun him with Anivia Q Flash Frost and follow up with Anivia E Frostbite. Use Anivia W Crystallize to separate Ekko from his follow-up, placing the wall so it does not block allies who are engaging.
Ekko.watch: When you see the indicator for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, stay out of the marked area. Stuns and shields are possible inside, making it dangerous. Watch the direction Ekko Q Timewinder travels and step aside from its return path too.

Fizz.watch: Fizz E Playful / Trickster is used both to engage and escape, so save Anivia Q Flash Frost until it has been fully spent. If the fish from Fizz R Chum the Waters attaches to you, move away from allies before the shark erupts.
Fizz.build: Fizz deals mostly magic damage, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Survive the early game with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Fizz.fight: Counterattack with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize right after Fizz E Playful / Trickster is used. If Fizz Q Urchin Strike is also down, block his escape with a wall, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not use Anivia E Frostbite on an unchilled target.
Fizz.laning: Look for a trade when Fizz misses a last hit with the empowered basic attack from Fizz W Seastone Trident, putting it on its full cooldown. After learning Anivia R Glacial Storm, use it to push the wave only for a purpose such as roaming or securing vision, then turn it off immediately.
Fizz.combo: For a basic trade, land Anivia Q Flash Frost, recast it to stun, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Fizz E Playful / Trickster is down and you can block his escape, follow with Anivia W Crystallize, the detonation of Anivia Q Flash Frost, then Anivia E Frostbite. When using Anivia R Glacial Storm, place it early and let it reach full size before using Anivia E Frostbite.
Fizz.escape: The window for Anivia to counterattack opens after Fizz E Playful / Trickster has been fully spent. Check whether Fizz Q Urchin Strike is also down, then catch him with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize. If only one mobility ability is down, he can escape with the other, so do not rush the engage.
Fizz.phase: In the late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Fizz.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. Stay close to your allies to draw out Fizz E Playful / Trickster, then catch him with Anivia Q Flash Frost once it has been fully spent and focus him down. Use Anivia W Crystallize to separate Fizz from his follow-up, but do not block allies who are engaging.

Galio.watch: Dodge Galio E Justice Punch when you see him step back to wind up. Charging Galio W Shield of Durand reduces the damage he takes and lengthens the taunt, so walk out of taunt range instead of using Anivia E Frostbite. Avoid the point where the two gusts of Galio Q Winds of War meet.
Galio.build: Galio deals mostly magic damage, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Survive the early game with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Galio.fight: Anivia has no mobility ability to escape, so stay out of range of Galio E Justice Punch and Galio W Shield of Durand. After Galio W Shield of Durand is used, land Anivia Q Flash Frost and take a short trade with Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite.
Galio.laning: If Galio spends mana using abilities to clear the wave, push the lane to give him less room to influence another lane with Galio R Hero's Entrance. Use Anivia R Glacial Storm to clear the wave only when you intend to roam or secure vision afterward.
Galio.combo: Block Galio's escape with Anivia W Crystallize, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. Anivia Q Flash Frost must chill him for Anivia E Frostbite to deal double damage. If you placed Anivia R Glacial Storm first, wait until it reaches full size before using Anivia E Frostbite.
Galio.escape: If only Galio E Justice Punch is down, he can escape with Galio R Hero's Entrance, so do not immediately go too deep. Before Galio R Hero's Entrance comes back up, especially when his engage abilities are down, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and look to land Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Galio.phase: In the late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Galio.teamfight: From well behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. If you see the landing marker for Galio R Hero's Entrance, immediately walk out of its area. When Galio begins his engage, use Anivia W Crystallize to cut off his follow-up, then hit the enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

Irelia.watch: Irelia Q Bladesurge can carry her through low-health minions to close the gap repeatedly, so back away when minions are about to die. Watch for the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet and the barrier from Irelia R Vanguard's Edge. If trapped inside the barrier, wait for it to disappear instead of crossing the blades.
Irelia.build: Survive the early game with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Irelia deals mostly physical damage, and Anivia has relatively low armor, so build armor first. If the healing from Irelia Q Bladesurge keeps offsetting the damage over time from Anivia R Glacial Storm, reduce her healing with Morellonomicon.
Irelia.fight: Right after Irelia Q Bladesurge is used is your chance to close the gap or lock her down. Recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to stun her, then use Anivia E Frostbite on the chilled Irelia. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not force Anivia E Frostbite.
Irelia.laning: Irelia can close the gap through low-health minions between you and her, so do not leave those minions alive, and back away when they are about to die. Save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop her engage rather than poke, and save Anivia W Crystallize as well when the lane is pushed.
Irelia.combo: When Irelia Q Bladesurge is down, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If you can place Anivia R Glacial Storm in advance, let it reach full size before using Anivia E Frostbite on the chilled Irelia.
Irelia.escape: Right after Irelia Q Bladesurge is used, catch her with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize. If the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet is also down, look for a trade during that window.
Irelia.phase: In the late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Irelia.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. When Irelia engages, cut off her follow-up with Anivia W Crystallize and prioritize Irelia with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. The wall is especially effective at separating enemies in narrow passages.

Hwei.watch: If the root or forced movement from Hwei E Subject: Torment catches you, follow-up abilities are likely to hit, so do not approach recklessly while it is available. If the first ability hits, move immediately to avoid the second ability and the explosion from Hwei P Signature of the Visionary. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster deals damage based on maximum or missing health, so keep your distance especially when low on health.
Hwei.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Hwei deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first on Anivia. Because Hwei Q Subject: Disaster scales with maximum health, prioritize resistances and movement speed over simply adding health.
Hwei.fight: Right after Hwei E Subject: Torment is used to poke or clear the wave is your chance to close the gap. Block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize, land Anivia Q Flash Frost, then deal damage with Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not waste Anivia E Frostbite on an unchilled enemy.
Hwei.laning: Save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop Hwei's engage or use it with an angle created by Anivia W Crystallize, rather than for poke.
Hwei.combo: Place Anivia W Crystallize across Hwei's escape route, then recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall and use Anivia E Frostbite on the chilled Hwei. If you have set up the fight in advance, place Anivia R Glacial Storm first, let it reach full size, then follow with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.
Hwei.escape: Hwei has no mobility ability, so right after he uses Hwei E Subject: Torment is your window to engage. Block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize, stun him with Anivia Q Flash Frost, then finish with Anivia E Frostbite. If Hwei E Subject: Torment is still available, wait; its root or forced movement could stop your engage.
Hwei.phase: In the late game, control Hwei's movement routes and the fight terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Hwei.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. Avoid passages Hwei has blocked with an area effect or an eye, and in narrow spaces use Anivia W Crystallize to separate Hwei's follow-up from him. Hit enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite, but do not engage first while Hwei E Subject: Torment is available.

Kassadin.watch: Kassadin Q Null Sphere grants a shield that absorbs magic damage, so use Anivia E Frostbite after the shield is gone.
Kassadin.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle to survive and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Kassadin deals primarily magic damage, so build magic resistance first.
Kassadin.fight: After Kassadin Q Null Sphere is down or immediately after he uses Kassadin R Riftwalk, apply chill with Anivia Q Flash Frost and trade with Anivia E Frostbite.
Kassadin.laning: Anivia lacks mana and damage early, so focus on last-hitting with basic attacks and Anivia E Frostbite instead of forcing a kill. If you push the lane, save Anivia W Crystallize in case of a gank. Unnecessary spells near Kassadin reduce the cooldown of Kassadin E Force Pulse, so clear waves from outside his range when possible.
Kassadin.combo: For a standard trade, hit Kassadin with Anivia Q Flash Frost, recast it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite while he is chilled. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite. When Kassadin R Riftwalk is down and you have a guaranteed opening, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite.
Kassadin.escape: If Kassadin runs out of mana during a chase and loses his way to escape, use Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize to catch him.
Kassadin.phase: Late game, watch for Kassadin R Riftwalk into your backline and control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Kassadin.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm at the fight location early and let it grow to full size. Kassadin can enter the backline, so do not stand alone within range of Kassadin R Riftwalk. After he enters, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate his follow-up. Stun enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost, then use Anivia E Frostbite on a chilled target.

Karma.watch: Repeated hits from Karma Q Inner Flame and Karma W Focused Resolve let her use Karma R Mantra more often through Karma P Gathering Fire. When a Karma Q Inner Flame empowered by Karma R Mantra creates an area on the ground, leave the circle before it explodes. Break the tether from Karma W Focused Resolve by moving out of range before it roots you.
Karma.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle to survive and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Karma's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. If healing from Karma W Focused Resolve empowered by Karma R Mantra keeps offsetting the damage over time from Anivia R Glacial Storm, buy Morellonomicon to reduce healing.
Karma.fight: Keep your distance while Karma W Focused Resolve is available, and fight after breaking its tether or drawing out the spell. In trades, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost to apply chill, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If a shield from Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra has been applied, engage after it expires.
Karma.laning: Save Anivia Q Flash Frost for stopping ganks and guaranteed openings rather than poke. Dodge Karma Q Inner Flame from behind minions or outside its range. If you push the lane, save Anivia W Crystallize in case of a gank.
Karma.combo: Block Karma's escape with Anivia W Crystallize, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite because it will not be empowered. In a fight where you place Anivia R Glacial Storm first and let it reach full size, use Anivia E Frostbite on chilled Karma.
Karma.escape: After Karma W Focused Resolve is down, you can close the distance without worrying about its root. Once the movement speed boost has ended and the shield is gone from Karma E Inspire or Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize and detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Karma.phase: In mid game, as your mana problems ease, make use of sustained damage. Late game, control the terrain with your wall and storm.
Karma.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm at the fight location early and let it grow. If Karma W Focused Resolve is available, create distance first to draw it out. Attack after the shield from Karma E Inspire empowered by Karma R Mantra is gone. When the enemy engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate their follow-up, then hit enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

Leblanc.watch: When LeBlanc Q Sigil of Malice marks you, her next spell deals more damage, so back away until the mark expires. If LeBlanc E Ethereal Chains hits you, move out of range immediately before the tether roots you. Watch the engage range of LeBlanc W Distortion as well.
Leblanc.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first early on and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. LeBlanc deals mostly magic damage, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Leblanc.fight: When LeBlanc engages with LeBlanc W Distortion, keep your distance and save Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize to respond. After the return from LeBlanc W Distortion expires or is used, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize and detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost to counterattack. Use Anivia E Frostbite after applying chill.
Leblanc.laning: If you push the lane, save Anivia W Crystallize. Back away when LeBlanc Q Sigil of Malice marks you. Alert your team immediately when LeBlanc disappears from vision.
Leblanc.combo: For a standard trade, hit with Anivia Q Flash Frost, recast it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite. After the return from LeBlanc W Distortion expires or is used, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite.
Leblanc.escape: Immediately after forcing LeBlanc W Distortion, you have an opening to close the distance, but watch whether she returns while she can still go back to her original position. If the return has expired or already been used and you have avoided the root from LeBlanc E Ethereal Chains, catch her with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Leblanc.phase: Late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Leblanc.teamfight: From well behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm at the fight location early and let it reach full size. When LeBlanc engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate her follow-up, then use Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite on enemies left in front. Fight in narrow passages, but do not block your allies' entry path with the wall.

Lux.watch: If Lux Q Light Binding hits you, her follow-up abilities are easier to land. Avoid standing in line with an ally and dodge sideways. If a Lux ability hits you, back away so she cannot trigger Lux P Illumination with an auto attack. When you see the targeting line for Lux R Final Spark, move sideways instead of retreating in a straight line.
Lux.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Lux's magic damage. Choose Mercury's Treads for boots and build magic resistance.
Lux.fight: Bait and dodge Lux Q Light Binding, then close the distance. Hit with Anivia Q Flash Frost to chill Lux, reactivate it to stun her, then use Anivia E Frostbite for empowered damage. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not use Anivia E Frostbite.
Lux.laning: If you push the wave, save Anivia W Crystallize for your escape.
Lux.combo: After Lux Q Light Binding misses, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize. Reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall to detonate it, then hit the stunned Lux with Anivia E Frostbite. If you placed Anivia R Glacial Storm early and let it reach full size, use Anivia E Frostbite for empowered damage against the chilled Lux.
Lux.escape: The moment Lux Q Light Binding misses is your chance to close the distance. Lux has no mobility ability, so once you reach her, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize and detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Lux.phase: Late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Lux.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. Do not group with allies where Lux E Lucent Singularity can trap you together. When the engage begins, use Anivia W Crystallize to cut off enemy reinforcements. Follow up on the enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

Lissandra.watch: Lissandra Q Ice Shard passes through its first target, so do not stand in line with allied minions. Keep your distance: if Lissandra W Ring of Frost roots you or Lissandra R Frozen Tomb stuns you, follow-up damage is easy to land. While Lissandra E Glacial Path is traveling, stun her with Anivia Q Flash Frost before she reactivates it to prevent the movement.
Lissandra.build: Early on, withstand her damage with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads. Lissandra deals mostly magic damage, and Anivia is vulnerable to follow-up damage after a root or stun, so prioritize magic resistance and tenacity. If Lissandra's self-healing keeps offsetting the damage over time from Anivia R Glacial Storm, reduce her healing with Morellonomicon.
Lissandra.fight: Anivia has no escape ability, so keep your distance first. Trade right after Lissandra W Ring of Frost is used on the wave or misses. After she uses Lissandra E Glacial Path, close the distance and limit her escape with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize. If Lissandra R Frozen Tomb is available, spread out your damage so you can continue attacking after the stasis from casting it on herself ends.
Lissandra.laning: Stand at an angle to your allied minions to avoid the path of Lissandra Q Ice Shard after it passes through them. Once you learn Anivia R Glacial Storm, push the wave when you have a purpose, such as roaming or gaining vision, then turn it off immediately.
Lissandra.combo: For a basic trade, hit with Anivia Q Flash Frost, reactivate it to detonate it, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Lissandra E Glacial Path is down, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, then follow with Anivia E Frostbite. If you placed Anivia R Glacial Storm early, wait until it reaches full size before using Anivia E Frostbite for empowered damage.
Lissandra.escape: Right after Lissandra uses Lissandra E Glacial Path is your window to close the distance. If she also uses Lissandra W Ring of Frost on the wave or misses it, approach and trap her with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize. If Lissandra E Glacial Path is still traveling, try to stun her with Anivia Q Flash Frost before she reactivates it.
Lissandra.phase: Late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Lissandra.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. Watch whether Lissandra has used Lissandra E Glacial Path. When the enemy engages, separate their reinforcements with Anivia W Crystallize, then hit the enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. In narrow passages, Anivia W Crystallize can cut off their path.

Naafiri.watch: If one Naafiri Q Darkin Daggers hits you, keep your distance until the bleed ends to avoid the second hit. Do not give Naafiri an angle to close in with Naafiri E Eviscerate, and do not travel alone when Naafiri R Hounds' Pursuit is available. Save targeted abilities while Naafiri W The Call of the Pack is active.
Naafiri.build: Naafiri deals mostly physical damage, and Anivia has low armor, so buy Cloth Armor first to withstand her damage. Choose Plated Steelcaps and prioritize armor.
Naafiri.fight: Clear Naafiri's pack with area abilities, but use the moment right after Naafiri E Eviscerate revives the pack to counterattack. Do not go too deep while Naafiri still has multiple mobility abilities available. Chill and stun her with Anivia Q Flash Frost, then deal damage with Anivia E Frostbite.
Naafiri.laning: Early on, farm from behind your minion line and do not give Naafiri an angle to close in with Naafiri E Eviscerate. Save Anivia Q Flash Frost to respond to an engage rather than for poke, and last-hit with auto attacks and Anivia E Frostbite. If you push the wave, save Anivia W Crystallize to block the path behind you as you escape.
Naafiri.combo: For a trade, hit with Anivia Q Flash Frost, reactivate it to detonate it, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If you can block the escape route, place a wall with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of it, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not waste Anivia E Frostbite on an unchilled target.
Naafiri.escape: Before Naafiri R Hounds' Pursuit comes back up is your chance to engage. Do not go in just because one Naafiri Q Darkin Daggers is down; check her remaining mobility options, including Naafiri E Eviscerate. When those options are down, limit her escape with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize.
Naafiri.phase: Late game, fight as a group and control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Naafiri.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. When Naafiri engages, separate her reinforcements with Anivia W Crystallize and attack the enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. Right after an ally falls, watch for Naafiri R Hounds' Pursuit again and retreat together.

Malzahar.watch: When a minion affected by Malzahar E Malefic Visions dies, it spreads to a nearby target, so do not wait beside that minion to last-hit. When you see Malzahar Q Call of the Void, move outside the line between its portals to avoid the silence. While Malzahar R Nether Grasp is available, do not pass through areas without vision alone, where he can catch you by yourself.
Malzahar.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads early on. Malzahar's main damage is magic, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Malzahar.fight: If Malzahar P Void Shift is active, remove it first with Anivia W Crystallize or Anivia Q Flash Frost. Once it is gone, hit with Anivia Q Flash Frost, reactivate it to stun him, then trade with Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite and keep your distance.
Malzahar.laning: When Malzahar pushes the wave, create a chance to catch him with your jungler and remove Malzahar P Void Shift first.
Malzahar.combo: Remove Malzahar P Void Shift first, then block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall. If you placed Anivia R Glacial Storm first, use Anivia E Frostbite after the storm reaches full size.
Malzahar.escape: After you dodge Malzahar Q Call of the Void and remove Malzahar P Void Shift, you have a chance to engage. Malzahar has no ability to create distance on his own, so block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and hit him with Anivia Q Flash Frost. Do not engage alone if Malzahar R Nether Grasp is available.
Malzahar.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. If Malzahar W Void Swarm minions are already out, clear them first with area abilities, then separate Malzahar's reinforcements with Anivia W Crystallize. If an ally is caught by Malzahar R Nether Grasp, interrupt the channel by applying crowd control that prevents Malzahar from moving.
Malzahar.phase: What Malzahar builds up with Malzahar W Void Swarm grows stronger over time, so deny him chances to build it up early. Late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.

Mel.watch: Mel W Rebuttal reflects projectiles, so do not cast Anivia Q Flash Frost when it looks about to activate. Mel E Solar Snare roots you if its center hits, so dodge sideways and watch for Mel Q Radiant Volley after the root. If several of Mel's attacks have built up Overwhelm stacks, back off even if you still have health. After leaving the fight, watch for Mel R Golden Eclipse until the stacks expire.
Mel.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Mel's magic damage early. Choose Mercury's Treads and prioritize magic resistance.
Mel.fight: When Mel W Rebuttal is down, hit Mel with Anivia Q Flash Frost and recast it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite on her while she is chilled. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not force Anivia E Frostbite. Mel has no ability to create distance, so after dodging Mel E Solar Snare, use Anivia W Crystallize to block her retreat and pressure her.
Mel.laning: When Mel W Rebuttal or Mel E Solar Snare is down, apply brief pressure to limit her chances to scale.
Mel.combo: When Mel W Rebuttal is down, block her retreat with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall to stun her, then use Anivia E Frostbite. In teamfights, place Anivia R Glacial Storm first, let it grow to full size, then follow with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. Mel W Rebuttal cannot reflect an area effect already on the ground, so you can place Anivia R Glacial Storm first.
Mel.escape: Dodge Mel E Solar Snare sideways, then close the distance once Mel W Rebuttal is also down. Mel has no ability to create distance, so block her retreat with Anivia W Crystallize and look to land Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Mel.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. When the enemy engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate their follow-up, then use Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite on the enemies left in front. Draw fights into narrow passages, but take care not to block your allies' entry path with Anivia W Crystallize.

Orianna.watch: Track where Orianna places her ball with Orianna Q Command: Attack, and do not linger near it. Near the ball, Orianna R Command: Shockwave can pull you in; also watch for the slow from Orianna W Command: Dissonance. Avoid extended basic attack trades early because of Orianna P Clockwork Windup.
Orianna.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Orianna's damage is mostly magic, and Anivia's magic resistance is relatively low, so prioritize magic resistance.
Orianna.fight: Try to trade just after Orianna moves her ball away from herself with Orianna Q Command: Attack. Land Anivia Q Flash Frost and recast it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite on the chilled Orianna. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite.
Orianna.laning: Avoid taking consecutive basic attacks empowered by Orianna P Clockwork Windup, and save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop ganks and for reliable trading opportunities. If you have pushed the lane, save Anivia W Crystallize to protect your escape route.
Orianna.combo: Block Orianna's retreat with Anivia W Crystallize, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If you placed Anivia R Glacial Storm beforehand and let it reach full size, Anivia E Frostbite can deal its empowered damage to the chilled Orianna.
Orianna.escape: Just after Orianna sends her ball far away with Orianna Q Command: Attack is a chance to close the distance. If the slow from Orianna W Command: Dissonance and the displacement from Orianna R Command: Shockwave are down, block her retreat with Anivia W Crystallize and look to land Anivia Q Flash Frost. Orianna has no ability to create distance on her own.
Orianna.phase: Early on, Anivia lacks mana and damage, so focus on surviving instead of pressuring Orianna too hard. Later, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Orianna.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. Watch Orianna's ball and avoid positions where Orianna R Command: Shockwave could pull you in. When the enemy engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate their follow-up, then use Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite on the enemies left in front.

Qiyana.watch: Qiyana Q Elemental Wrath / Edge of Ixtal can root with the river element, so move out of range when she approaches holding it. Qiyana R Supreme Display of Talent explodes and stuns when it reaches terrain, so do not stand with your back to a wall or face her near the river or in narrow passages.
Qiyana.build: Qiyana's main damage is physical, and Anivia has low armor, so buy Cloth Armor first to survive. Choose Plated Steelcaps and prioritize armor.
Qiyana.fight: Anivia has no escape ability, so first manage the engage range of Qiyana W Terrashape and Qiyana E Audacity. When both mobility abilities are down and Qiyana is left in front of you, stun her with Anivia Q Flash Frost, then counterattack with Anivia E Frostbite.
Qiyana.laning: Early on, prioritize last hits and levels over kills, and save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop Qiyana's engage rather than poke her. If you have pushed the lane, also save Anivia W Crystallize to escape. Use Anivia R Glacial Storm to clear a wave only when you intend to push and move or gain vision.
Qiyana.combo: Before Qiyana E Audacity comes back up, block her retreat with Anivia W Crystallize, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite rather than using it without its empowered damage.
Qiyana.escape: Do not rush in when only Qiyana W Terrashape is down, because she can escape with Qiyana E Audacity. Once both mobility abilities are down, especially before Qiyana E Audacity comes back up, trap her with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize.
Qiyana.phase: Qiyana is strongest in the mid game, so avoid giving her an advantage then and build armor. Later, stay grouped and control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Qiyana.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow to full size. Stand away from walls to avoid giving Qiyana an opening for Qiyana R Supreme Display of Talent. When the enemy engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate their follow-up, then attack the enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

Ryze.watch: If Ryze E Spell Flux hits you, move away from allies until the mark expires. Once marked, Ryze W Rune Prison roots you and Ryze Q Overload deals increased damage, so dodge Ryze E Spell Flux first. When you see Ryze R Realm Warp, watch its arrival point and interrupt Ryze with the stun from Anivia Q Flash Frost before it activates.
Ryze.build: Ryze deals primarily magic damage, so build magic resistance first. Buy Null-Magic Mantle early and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Ryze.fight: Land Anivia Q Flash Frost to chill Ryze, then use Anivia E Frostbite for a short trade. When Ryze R Realm Warp is unavailable, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost to create an opening to engage.
Ryze.laning: Ryze also lacks mana and damage early, so pressure him when you can safely land Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Ryze.combo: For a standard trade, land Anivia Q Flash Frost, reactivate it to detonate it, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia W Crystallize can block Ryze's escape, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall and follow with Anivia E Frostbite. Save Anivia E Frostbite if Anivia Q Flash Frost misses.
Ryze.escape: If you dodge Ryze E Spell Flux, Ryze W Rune Prison only slows instead of rooting. Confirm that before trading.
Ryze.phase: Late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Ryze.teamfight: From behind your frontline, cast Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it reach maximum size. When Ryze comes in, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate the enemies following him in, then hit the enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. If Ryze E Spell Flux marks you, move away from allies to avoid the spreading damage from Ryze Q Overload.

Syndra.watch: If Syndra Q Dark Sphere lies between you and Syndra, move out of its line so Syndra E Scatter the Weak cannot push it into you and stun you. Move away from areas where Syndra has placed several Syndra Q Dark Spheres, since Syndra R Unleashed Power is dangerous there. Watch for the slow and true damage from Syndra W Force of Will, and walk out of the areas targeted by Syndra Q Dark Sphere, Syndra W Force of Will, and Syndra E Scatter the Weak.
Syndra.build: Early on, first get Null-Magic Mantle to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against Syndra's main damage, but also consider your total health against the true damage from Syndra W Force of Will and the execute from Syndra R Unleashed Power.
Syndra.fight: When Syndra E Scatter the Weak is unavailable, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize and look for a chance to land Anivia Q Flash Frost. In trades, chill her with Anivia Q Flash Frost before using Anivia E Frostbite. Save Anivia E Frostbite if Anivia Q Flash Frost misses.
Syndra.laning: Save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop a gank or for a reliable opening rather than using it to poke. If you push the lane, keep Anivia W Crystallize available for an escape. After learning Anivia R Glacial Storm, use it to clear waves only when you intend to push and roam or establish vision.
Syndra.combo: While Syndra E Scatter the Weak is unavailable, block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize, reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. Anivia E Frostbite deals double damage when the target is chilled by Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Syndra.escape: Syndra E Scatter the Weak has a long cooldown and is her only self-defense tool, so engage right after she uses it. Syndra has no mobility ability; block her escape with Anivia W Crystallize and look to stun her with Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Syndra.phase: Late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Syndra.teamfight: From well behind your frontline, cast Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will begin and let it reach maximum size. Avoid areas with several Syndra Q Dark Spheres. When the enemy engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to cut off the enemies following them in. Hit enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

Sylas.watch: The chain thrown after the initial dash of Sylas E Abscond / Abduct is more dangerous than the dash itself. Sylas W Kingslayer heals him more when his health is low, so do not delay finishing him off.
Sylas.build: Build magic resistance first against Sylas's main damage. Survive the early game with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. If the healing from Sylas W Kingslayer keeps offsetting the damage over time from Anivia R Glacial Storm, buy Morellonomicon.
Sylas.fight: Reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it, then use Anivia E Frostbite on the chilled Sylas. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, hold Anivia E Frostbite and wait for another chance.
Sylas.laning: Early on, focus on last hits and keeping up in levels instead of forcing a kill. If you push the lane, save Anivia W Crystallize to stop Sylas from engaging or to prevent a gank.
Sylas.combo: Block Sylas's escape with Anivia W Crystallize, reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If you cast Anivia R Glacial Storm first, wait until it reaches maximum size before following with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. Right after Sylas dashes in with Sylas E Abscond / Abduct, stun him with Anivia Q Flash Frost and attack before he can heal with Sylas W Kingslayer.
Sylas.escape: Sylas W Kingslayer is also a mobility ability, so do not overcommit to a chase just because Sylas E Abscond / Abduct is unavailable. Once he has used both mobility abilities, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and land Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Sylas.phase: Late game, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Sylas.teamfight: From behind your frontline, cast Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow. If Sylas engages with Sylas E Abscond / Abduct, stun him with Anivia Q Flash Frost and use Anivia W Crystallize to separate the enemies following him in. Confirm that an enemy trapped in front is chilled before using Anivia E Frostbite.

Talon.watch: If the outgoing hit of Talon W Rake lands, move out of its return path: taking both hits can trigger Talon P Blade's End. Watch the dash range of Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy and the stealth from Talon R Shadow Assault. Do not overcommit to a chase while Talon R Shadow Assault is available.
Talon.build: Survive the early game with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Talon deals physical damage, so build armor first. If Talon has flat penetration, build health as well.
Talon.fight: Early on, save Anivia Q Flash Frost for Talon's engage instead of starting fights. Right after Talon uses Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and counterattack by stunning him with Anivia Q Flash Frost. You can also counterattack after he has used Talon R Shadow Assault.
Talon.laning: Last-hit with basic attacks and save Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize for engages and ganks. After learning Anivia R Glacial Storm, push the wave when you intend to keep Talon from roaming or establish vision, and share his location with your team.
Talon.combo: If Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy is unavailable, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize, reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not force an unempowered Anivia E Frostbite. If you cast Anivia R Glacial Storm in advance and let it reach maximum size, use an empowered Anivia E Frostbite on enemies inside it as well.
Talon.escape: Right after you draw out Talon Q Noxian Diplomacy is your opening to pick him off. Dodge the return path of Talon W Rake, then block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and stun him with Anivia Q Flash Frost. It is an even better time to counterattack if you confirm that Talon R Shadow Assault has also been used.
Talon.phase: Talon's impact falls off late game, so fight by controlling the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Talon.teamfight: From behind your frontline, cast Anivia R Glacial Storm where the fight will happen and let it grow. If Talon dives your backline, stay grouped with allies and stun him with Anivia Q Flash Frost, then use Anivia W Crystallize to separate anyone following him in. Use Anivia E Frostbite on chilled enemies, and fight in narrow passages when possible.

Veigar.watch: Veigar E Event Horizon stuns when you cross its edge. If trapped inside, move around instead of running into the edge, and sidestep Veigar W Dark Matter when its landing spot appears. If you fall below half health, move out of range of Veigar R Primordial Burst, which grows stronger based on your missing health.
Veigar.build: Veigar deals mostly magic damage, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Survive the early game with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots.
Veigar.fight: Hit Veigar with Anivia Q Flash Frost to chill him, then trade with Anivia E Frostbite. Once Veigar E Event Horizon is down, use Anivia W Crystallize to block his retreat and detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost for a chance to engage.
Veigar.laning: Dodge Veigar Q Baleful Strike and look for chances to slow his scaling, but save Anivia Q Flash Frost for a reliable hit or to stop a gank. If you push the wave, keep Anivia W Crystallize available to protect your escape route.
Veigar.combo: For a basic trade, hit with Anivia Q Flash Frost, recast it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If you can block Veigar's retreat, use Anivia W Crystallize → Anivia Q Flash Frost → Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not waste Anivia E Frostbite on an unchilled target.
Veigar.escape: Engage Veigar just after he uses Veigar E Event Horizon. Veigar has no ability to create distance, so block his retreat with Anivia W Crystallize and catch him with Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Veigar.phase: Both champions are weak early, but there are chances to pressure Veigar before he has stacks. Later, Veigar P Phenomenal Evil Power stacks make the matchup increasingly unfavorable, so fight while tracking Veigar's position and whether he has used Veigar E Event Horizon.
Veigar.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow. Check Veigar's position and Veigar E Event Horizon, then use Anivia W Crystallize to separate the follow-up enemies when they engage. Once the storm reaches full size, finish off enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

TwistedFate.watch: Once Twisted Fate locks in a gold card with Twisted Fate W Pick a Card, one basic attack will stun you, so stay outside his basic attack range. Twisted Fate Q Wild Cards is area poke; reduce the damage you take by staying behind minions.
TwistedFate.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Twisted Fate deals mostly magic damage, and Anivia has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
TwistedFate.fight: Early on, Anivia should farm and hold on instead of forcing fights. Look to engage when Twisted Fate has used the gold card from Twisted Fate W Pick a Card and cannot use Twisted Fate R Destiny. Then block his retreat with Anivia W Crystallize, hit Anivia Q Flash Frost, and deal damage with Anivia E Frostbite.
TwistedFate.laning: Do not use Anivia Q Flash Frost freely for poke; save it to stop a gank or for a reliable attack. Last-hit with basic attacks and Anivia E Frostbite, but do not waste mana using Anivia E Frostbite on an unchilled opponent.
TwistedFate.combo: For a basic trade, hit Twisted Fate with Anivia Q Flash Frost and recast it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite on him while he is chilled. If you can block his retreat, put up a wall with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of it, then follow with Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite.
TwistedFate.escape: Just after Twisted Fate uses the gold card from Twisted Fate W Pick a Card, you can engage without worrying about the stun.
TwistedFate.phase: Anivia comes into her strength in the mid game once her mana issues ease. In the late game, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
TwistedFate.teamfight: From behind her frontline, Anivia should place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow. When enemies engage, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate their follow-up, then hit the enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. If you see Twisted Fate use Twisted Fate R Destiny within range, interrupt his teleport with Anivia Q Flash Frost or Anivia W Crystallize.

Vex.watch: When the fear from Vex P Doom 'n Gloom is ready, do not force a fight within Vex's ability range. Vex E Looming Darkness grows wider the farther it travels, so if you are dodging it within range, take a short step sideways instead of retreating a long way. If Vex R Shadow Surge hits you, move toward your allies and counter Vex's incoming dash with Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Vex.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Vex deals mostly magic damage, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Vex.fight: For a basic trade, hit with Anivia Q Flash Frost and recast it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite. Look for a window when both the fear from Vex P Doom 'n Gloom and the shield from Vex W Personal Space are down. Then block Vex's retreat with Anivia W Crystallize and detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Vex.laning: If you push the wave, save Anivia W Crystallize for your escape.
Vex.combo: Put Anivia W Crystallize on Vex's retreat path, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. In teamfights, place Anivia R Glacial Storm first and let it reach full size before following up with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.
Vex.escape: If Vex uses the fear from Vex P Doom 'n Gloom on the wave or for poke and the shield from Vex W Personal Space is also down, catch her with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Vex.phase: In the late game, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Vex.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow. When Vex engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate her follow-up, then attack enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. Low-health allies should move out of Vex's range first so a first kill from Vex R Shadow Surge does not lead to chain damage.

Viktor.watch: Viktor E Hextech Ray travels in a line, so avoid standing in line with the wave and step sideways. When Viktor W Gravity Field appears, leave it immediately to avoid the stun, and do not keep trading inside it.
Viktor.build: In the early game, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Viktor deals mostly magic damage, and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first.
Viktor.fight: Keep a safe distance, then look for an angle to hit Anivia Q Flash Frost after leaving Viktor W Gravity Field. Viktor controls the fight better up close but has no dash to escape on his own, so fight when you have a reliable angle to block his retreat with Anivia W Crystallize.
Viktor.laning: Do not use Anivia Q Flash Frost carelessly for poke; save it to stop a gank or for a guaranteed hit. Look for opportunities before Viktor's scaling from Viktor P Glorious Evolution builds up, but prioritize scaling safely over forcing trades.
Viktor.combo: Put Anivia W Crystallize on Viktor's retreat path, recast Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not use Anivia E Frostbite without the chill. In teamfights, place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time and let it reach full size before following with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.
Viktor.escape: Look for an engage when Viktor W Gravity Field is down. Viktor has no ability to create distance on his own, so close the gap, block his retreat with Anivia W Crystallize, and hit him with Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Viktor.phase: Viktor's accumulated scaling puts you at a disadvantage in the late game, so control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Viktor.teamfight: From well behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow. When enemies engage, use Anivia W Crystallize to cut off their follow-up, then hit enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. Position yourself so you do not remain inside Viktor W Gravity Field.

Vladimir.watch: When Vladimir charges Vladimir E Tides of Blood, put minions between you or move out of range. Vladimir W Sanguine Pool deletes incoming projectiles, so save Anivia Q Flash Frost until the pool ends. If Vladimir R Hemoplague hits you, back off until its increased-damage effect ends and avoid grouping with allies.
Vladimir.build: Start with Null-Magic Mantle to survive the early game and choose Mercury's Treads. Vladimir deals mostly magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If Vladimir's healing offsets the damage over time from Anivia R Glacial Storm, use Morellonomicon to reduce his healing.
Vladimir.fight: After Vladimir W Sanguine Pool is down, stun him with Anivia Q Flash Frost and follow with Anivia E Frostbite. Save key abilities while his pool is available, and use the slow from charging Vladimir E Tides of Blood as an opening. In fights that keep him inside Anivia R Glacial Storm for a long time, watch out for his healing.
Vladimir.laning: Pressure Vladimir during his weak early game when you have a clear chance to land Anivia Q Flash Frost or set up a gank. If you push the lane, keep Anivia W Crystallize available in case of a gank.
Vladimir.combo: After Vladimir W Sanguine Pool ends, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize. Reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite because it will not deal its empowered damage.
Vladimir.escape: The moment Vladimir W Sanguine Pool ends is your chance to engage. He has no way out afterward, so trap him with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize. You can also close the distance while charging Vladimir E Tides of Blood slows him.
Vladimir.phase: Both champions are weak early, but take clear opportunities to pressure and gank Vladimir before he scales. Later, respect his scaling and control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Vladimir.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow. When Vladimir engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to split off those following him, then follow up with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite after his pool ends. Spread out so Vladimir R Hemoplague does not hit several allies; if infected, regroup after its effect ends.

Xerath.watch: Xerath Q Arcanopulse passes through minions, so when you see him charging it, change direction and dodge well to the side. Be especially careful to avoid Xerath E Shocking Orb, since its stun sets up follow-up attacks. Start dodging as soon as you see Xerath cast Xerath R Rite of the Arcane.
Xerath.build: Buy Null-Magic Mantle first to survive the early game. Xerath's main damage is magic and Anivia has relatively low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance and choose Mercury's Treads.
Xerath.fight: Close the distance right after Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction are used. Xerath has no mobility ability, so block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize, land Anivia Q Flash Frost, then trade with Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite.
Xerath.laning: Early on, focus on CS and levels rather than kills. Against Xerath's poke, focus on avoiding heavy damage; when mana is depleted, push the lane and call your jungler. Even after learning Anivia R Glacial Storm, use it to clear waves only when you intend to roam or establish vision, and turn it off as soon as that is done.
Xerath.combo: Place Anivia W Crystallize in Xerath's escape path, then reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost to detonate it in front of the wall and follow with Anivia E Frostbite. Anivia Q Flash Frost must chill him for Anivia E Frostbite to deal double damage.
Xerath.escape: Engage Xerath right after he uses Xerath E Shocking Orb and Xerath W Eye of Destruction. He has no mobility ability, so close the distance and cut off his escape with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia Q Flash Frost. When pushing the lane, keep Anivia W Crystallize available in case of a gank.
Xerath.phase: Later, control the terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Xerath.teamfight: Stay well behind your frontline and place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen, letting it reach full size. When the enemy engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to split off those following them, then hit the enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. In narrow passages, position the wall to split the enemy without blocking your allies' path in.

Zed.watch: Zed W Living Shadow is a mobility tool, so watch the shadow's position and move outside the slow radius of Zed E Shadow Slash. If Zed engages with Zed R Death Mark, stun him with Anivia Q Flash Frost to interrupt his follow-up damage before the mark detonates. Zed P Contempt for the Weak deals damage based on maximum health and is not blocked by armor.
Zed.build: In the early game, use Cloth Armor to withstand Zed's physical damage. Choose Plated Steelcaps and build armor first. Anivia's magic damage is effective against Zed's low magic resistance.
Zed.fight: Look for an opening after Zed W Living Shadow has been used, once the shadow disappears or Zed has already switched positions. Land Anivia Q Flash Frost to chill him, then deal damage with Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not use Anivia E Frostbite; if Zed R Death Mark is still available, do not rush the engage.
Zed.laning: Last-hit with basic attacks and Anivia E Frostbite when needed, and save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop Zed's engage. If you push the lane, keep Anivia W Crystallize available for your escape.
Zed.combo: When Zed's mobility is down, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize, reactivate Anivia Q Flash Frost to stun him in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. In teamfights, place Anivia R Glacial Storm first and let it reach full size before following with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite. A full-size storm can also chill enemies and empower Anivia E Frostbite.
Zed.escape: The opening comes after Zed uses Zed W Living Shadow, once the shadow disappears or he switches positions. If Zed R Death Mark is still available, he can use it to escape, so catch him with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize before it comes back.
Zed.phase: In the late game, Zed becomes weaker and Anivia's terrain control with her wall and storm becomes important, so stay grouped with your team as you move.
Zed.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow. When Zed engages, use Anivia Q Flash Frost to interrupt his follow-up damage before the mark detonates, and Anivia W Crystallize to split off the enemies following him. In narrow passages, finish off the enemies left in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

Yone.watch: If Yone repeatedly uses Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions, his whirlwind engage is ready, so keep your distance until the stacks expire. Save Anivia Q Flash Frost for his engage with Yone E Soul Unbound. In teamfights, Yone R Fate Sealed moves him behind the last champion in its path and pulls enemies together, so do not stand alone in the backline.
Yone.build: Anivia relies heavily on mana, so prioritize considering items that solve her mana problems. Yone deals both physical and magic damage, so do not rely on building only one type of resistance. Yone W Spirit Cleave deals damage based on maximum health, so also be wary of stacking health alone.
Yone.fight: Keep your distance when Yone's whirlwind engage is ready. After he enters with Yone E Soul Unbound, landing the stun from Anivia Q Flash Frost can prevent his return. To trade, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost to chill him, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite.
Yone.laning: When Yone repeatedly uses Yone Q Mortal Steel on minions to prepare his whirlwind, retreat out of range and save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop his engage. Even after learning Anivia R Glacial Storm, use it on the wave only when you intend to push and move or establish vision.
Yone.combo: The basic trade is Anivia Q Flash Frost → reactivate it to stun and chill → Anivia E Frostbite. If you can block Yone's escape, use Anivia W Crystallize → Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall → Anivia E Frostbite. If you placed Anivia R Glacial Storm in advance, let it reach full size before using its chill to empower Anivia E Frostbite.
Yone.escape: Do not engage just because Yone used one Yone Q Mortal Steel. Yone E Soul Unbound and Yone R Fate Sealed are also mobility tools, so look especially for the window before Yone R Fate Sealed comes back and block his escape with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize. If Yone enters in spirit form first, look for a chance to stop his return with the stun from Anivia Q Flash Frost.
Yone.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow. When Yone engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to split off those following him, then use Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite on the enemies left in front. The shield from Yone W Spirit Cleave grows with the number of champions it hits, so keep space between allies and avoid standing alone in the backline where Yone R Fate Sealed can reach you.

Zoe.watch: If Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble hits you, sleep takes effect shortly afterward. In that time, move behind an ally or a wall to get out of the angle and range of Zoe Q Paddle Star! When you see Zoe preparing to throw Zoe Q Paddle Star!, interrupt her redirect with Anivia Q Flash Frost or Anivia W Crystallize. A missed Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble remains as a trap, so be careful in narrow paths without vision.
Zoe.build: Early on, start by surviving with Null-Magic Mantle, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Zoe deals mostly magic damage, so prioritize magic resistance, but focus on dodging her bubble because of Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble's true damage and sleep follow-up.
Zoe.fight: Interrupt Zoe Q Paddle Star! with Anivia Q Flash Frost as she fires it. If it hits, reactivate it to detonate, then use Anivia E Frostbite. Zoe R Portal Jump always returns her to her starting point, so line up Anivia Q Flash Frost there.
Zoe.laning: Save Anivia Q Flash Frost to stop Zoe's approach or a gank, or use it when you have a sure angle. If you push the lane, keep Anivia W Crystallize available. Even after learning Anivia R Glacial Storm, use it to clear waves only when you intend to roam or secure vision.
Zoe.combo: When you have a sure angle, block Zoe's escape with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, then use Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, save Anivia E Frostbite rather than using it without Chill. If you placed Anivia R Glacial Storm in advance, wait for it to reach full size before following with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.
Zoe.escape: Look for a chance to approach right after Zoe E Sleepy Trouble Bubble is used, too.
Zoe.phase: In the late game, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Zoe.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow. If Zoe comes in with Zoe R Portal Jump, aim at the spot she will return to, and use Anivia W Crystallize to separate the enemies following her. In narrow passages, hit enemies trapped in front with Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite.

Yasuo.watch: Yasuo E Sweeping Blade uses minions to close the gap, so keep your distance when you're among minions. After Yasuo lands Yasuo Q Steel Tempest twice, his next attack knocks you airborne; watch for the sound and effect, then sidestep out of its line. Save Anivia Q Flash Frost while Yasuo W Wind Wall is in front of you, and use it once the wall disappears or you can go around it.
Yasuo.build: Survive the early game with Cloth Armor and choose Plated Steelcaps for boots. Yasuo deals mostly physical damage, and Anivia has low armor, so build armor first.
Yasuo.fight: Trigger the shield from Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer with a basic attack, then trade once its short duration ends. Right after dodging the tornado from Yasuo Q Steel Tempest, his airborne stacks reset; land Anivia Q Flash Frost and follow up with Anivia E Frostbite. If Anivia Q Flash Frost misses, do not use Anivia E Frostbite.
Yasuo.laning: Keep the wave thin and pushing toward your side to give Yasuo fewer minions to approach through with Yasuo E Sweeping Blade. If you push the lane, save Anivia W Crystallize and block off the area behind the direction of retreat to stop the engage.
Yasuo.combo: First remove the shield from Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer. Then land Anivia Q Flash Frost, reactivate it to detonate it, and use Anivia E Frostbite. When the hit is guaranteed, block his escape with Anivia W Crystallize, detonate Anivia Q Flash Frost in front of the wall, and follow up with Anivia E Frostbite. Save Anivia Q Flash Frost if Yasuo W Wind Wall is blocking it.
Yasuo.escape: The moment after dodging Yasuo Q Steel Tempest’s tornado is your chance to engage. Don’t go in just because Yasuo E Sweeping Blade is down; look to engage when Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia W Crystallize can lock him down before Yasuo R Last Breath comes back up.
Yasuo.phase: In the late game, control terrain with Anivia W Crystallize and Anivia R Glacial Storm.
Yasuo.teamfight: From behind your frontline, place Anivia R Glacial Storm ahead of time where the fight will happen and let it grow to full size. When Yasuo engages, use Anivia W Crystallize to separate those following him, then use Anivia Q Flash Frost and Anivia E Frostbite on the enemies left in front. Draw fights into narrow passages, but place the wall so it does not block allies who are engaging.
